'''Harold Philip Benson''' (born 1949) is an American operations researcher, mathematician, and professor. He is best known for his work in [[Multiple-criteria decision analysis|multiple-criteria decision making]] (MCDM)<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last1=Koksalan |first1=Murat |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HyW7CgAAQBAJ |title=Multiple Criteria Decision Making: From Early History To The 21st Century |last2=Wallenius |first2=Jyrki |last3=Zionts |first3=Stanley |date=2011-06-06 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-4462-23-5 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Martinovich |first=Milenko |date=2011-12-07 |title=Benson recognized as one of his field's top scholars in new book |url=https://news.warrington.ufl.edu/faculty-and-research/benson-recognized-as-one-of-his-fields-top-scholars-in-new-book/ |access-date=2023-04-15 |website=UF Warrington News |language=en-US}}</ref> and for formulating [[Benson's algorithm]] in the field of linear programming.<ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018">{{cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Guangya |last2=Li |first2=Shengjie |last3=Xu |first3=Jiuping |last4=Yang |first4=Xinmin |title=Dedication to Benson |journal=Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications |date=June 2018 |volume=177 |issue=3 |pages=606–608 |doi=10.1007/s10957-018-1315-4 |s2cid=254752917 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ehrgott |first1=Matthias |last2=Löhne |first2=Andreas |last3=Shao |first3=Lizhen |title=A dual variant of Benson's 'outer approximation algorithm' for multiple objective linear programming |journal=Journal of Global Optimization |date=April 2012 |volume=52 |issue=4 |pages=757–778 |doi=10.1007/s10898-011-9709-y |s2cid=254649300 }}</ref> He served as an American Economic Institutions professor at the [[University of Florida]].<ref name=":0" />

== Education ==
Benson graduated from the [[University of Michigan]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in Mathematics in 1971.<ref name=":0" /> He was a member of the university's [[Phi Beta Kappa]] chapter.<ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018"/> He also earned an [[Master of Science|M.S.]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[Industrial engineering|Industrial Engineering]] and the Management Sciences from [[Northwestern University]] in 1973 and 1976, respectively.<sup><ref name=":0" /><ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018"/></sup>

== Career ==
Benson worked as a research engineer at the [[Argonaut Building|General Motors Research Laboratory]] from 1976 to 1979.<ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018"/> After leaving his position at [[General Motors Research Laboratory]] in 1979, Benson was hired as a professor at the [[University of Florida]]’s [[Warrington College of Business]], where he taught until 2013.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018"/>

Benson has served as an associate editor for academic journals such as the ''[[Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications]]'', ''[[Naval Research Logistics]]'', and the ''Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications''.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tour |first=Schedule a Campus |title=Editorial Board Activity |url=https://warrington.ufl.edu/information-systems-and-operations-management-department/editorial-board-activity/ |access-date=2023-04-15 |website=Information Systems and Operations Management Department |language=en-US}}</ref> Benson was also a founding member of the multiple-criteria decision making section of the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]] (INFORMS) when it was established in 2010.<ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018"/>

== Research ==
Benson's research mainly concerns [[Multiple-criteria decision analysis|multiple-criteria decision making]] (MCDM), global optimization, and their applications.<ref name=":2" /><ref group=pub>{{cite journal |last1=Benson |first1=H. P. |title=Global Optimization Algorithm for the Nonlinear Sum of Ratios Problem |journal=Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications |date=January 2002 |volume=112 |issue=1 |pages=1–29 |doi=10.1023/A:1013072027218 |s2cid=121739598 }}</ref><ref group=pub>{{cite journal |last1=Benson |first1=H. P. |title=On the Global Optimization of Sums of Linear Fractional Functions over a Convex Set |journal=Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications |date=April 2004 |volume=121 |issue=1 |pages=19–39 |doi=10.1023/B:JOTA.0000026129.07165.5a |s2cid=120025863 }}</ref>

He invented what is now called [[Benson's algorithm]], which finds all of the efficient extreme points and the full weakly efficient set in the outcome set of a multiple objective linear program.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /><ref group=pub>{{cite journal |last1=Benson |first1=Harold P. |title=An Outer Approximation Algorithm for Generating All Efficient Extreme Points in the Outcome Set of a Multiple Objective Linear Programming Problem |journal=Journal of Global Optimization |date=1998 |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=1–24 |doi=10.1023/A:1008215702611 |s2cid=45440728 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-18351-5 |title=Vector Optimization with Infimum and Supremum |series=Vector Optimization |year=2011 |isbn=978-3-642-18350-8 |first1=Andreas |last1=Löhne |publisher=Springer|contribution=5.1 Benson's algorithm|pages=162–169}}</ref> A computer code called BENSOLVE was developed to execute this algorithm.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BENSOLVE - A Free Vector Linear Program Solver |url=https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~sa67leb/bensolve/ |access-date=2023-04-15 |website=users.fmi.uni-jena.de}}</ref>

Benson also helped to define and explore properly efficient solutions of nonlinear [[vector optimization]] problems.<ref group=pub>{{cite journal |last1=Benson |first1=Harold P |title=An improved definition of proper efficiency for vector maximization with respect to cones |journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications |date=September 1979 |volume=71 |issue=1 |pages=232–241 |doi=10.1016/0022-247X(79)90226-9 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref group=pub>{{cite journal |last1=Benson |first1=H. P. |title=Existence of efficient solutions for vector maximization problems |journal=Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications |date=December 1978 |volume=26 |issue=4 |pages=569–580 |doi=10.1007/BF00933152 |s2cid=121336616 }}</ref><ref group=pub>{{cite journal |last1=Benson |first1=Harold P |title=Efficiency and proper efficiency in vector maximization with respect to cones |journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications |date=April 1983 |volume=93 |issue=1 |pages=273–289 |doi=10.1016/0022-247X(83)90230-5 |doi-access=free }}</ref> In global optimization, he focused a good portion of his work on the theory and solutions for concave minimization problems.<ref group=pub>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-1-4615-2025-2_3 |chapter=Concave Minimization: Theory, Applications and Algorithms |title=Handbook of Global Optimization |series=Nonconvex Optimization and Its Applications |year=1995 |last1=Benson |first1=Harold P. |volume=2 |pages=43–148 |isbn=978-1-4613-5838-1 }}</ref><ref group=pub>{{cite journal |doi=10.1002/(SICI)1520-6750(199609)43:6<765::AID-NAV1>3.0.CO;2-2 |title=Deterministic algorithms for constrained concave minimization: A unified critical survey |year=1996 |last1=Benson |first1=Harold P. |journal=Naval Research Logistics |volume=43 |issue=6 |pages=765–795 }}</ref> During the 1990s, Benson's MCDM work included research on optimization over the efficient set and on generating the complete set of efficient and extreme point efficient solutions in the decision and criterion spaces of multiple objective mathematical programming problems.<ref name=":2" />

== Awards and honors ==
In 2004, Benson received the [[Georg Cantor]] Award from the International Society on Multiple Criteria Decision Making for his contributions to the theory, methodology, and practices of multiple-criteria decision making.<ref name=":2" /><sup><ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018"/></sup>

In the book ''Multiple Criteria Decision Making: From Early History to the 21st Century,'' which was published in 2011, Benson was named one of the 42 world-leading researchers in the history of MCDM.<sup><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /></sup>
In 2018, a special issue of the ''Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications'' was dedicated to Benson.<ref name="Chen Li Xu Yang 2018"/>
